_README: Hand-made ground truth for ONE video. EVALUATION ONLY. Nothing under src/excavator_cycles/ may import or read this file, and the pipeline must never open it -- reading the answer is explicitly disallowed by the task spec. See eval/README.md.

video._fps_note: The real rate, not 30. Treating this clip as 30 fps introduces a ~0.1% error in every duration -- small, but the task is graded at +/-0.6 s per field, so it is not free.
video._frame_count_note: 886 frames actually decode. The container header claims 1102, so cv2.CAP_PROP_FRAME_COUNT lies about this file by ~20%. The count above was obtained by demuxing the whole clip (grab() until it fails), which is what excavator_cycles.video.probe(verify=True) does.

provenance.source: hand-decided by Aanya from frame-by-frame inspection of the video
provenance.method: manual frame-by-frame review; these are NOT model outputs and were not produced by the pipeline

boundaries._units: Each value is an INSTANT BETWEEN FRAMES, not a frame index: boundary f means 'immediately before frame f'. A value may legitimately be 886 or larger, meaning 'after the final decoded frame'.
boundaries._definition_source: The four phase definitions come from the task spec. The four phases tile the cycle with no gaps: each phase ends immediately before the next phase begins. Only the four ONSETS are defined; no phase has an independently labelled end.
boundaries._cycle_ends_note: The onset of the NEXT digging phase, which is also where swinging ends and the one complete cycle closes.

_cycle_count_note: Exactly one complete cycle: f125 -> f880. Everything before f125 and everything after f880 is an incomplete partial cycle and is ignored, per the task spec.

durations._units: frames = (next onset - this onset). seconds_exact = frames / fps, kept at full precision for checking arithmetic. seconds = the graded value, what a correct answer.json should report.

expected_answer._note: The shape a correct answer.json takes, filled in with these labels. eval/score.py scores a candidate answer.json against exactly these five fields.

scoring._tolerance_note: +/-0.6 s per field, applied to the cycle average and to each of the four phase averages. cycle_count is an integer and must match exactly; a tolerance on a count is meaningless.

conventions: Boundaries are instants between frames, not frame indices. Phase duration in frames is the difference of two onsets, so no off-by-one correction is needed and none should be applied.
The four phases tile the cycle with no gaps. Only the four onsets are labelled; each phase ends exactly where the next begins, so the four phase durations sum to the cycle duration by construction.

Digging onset convention: the onset is marked +9 frames AFTER the bucket's teeth first touch the material. First touch for this cycle was observed at ~f116, so the labelled onset is f125. The offset exists because first contact is ambiguous to the eye across a frame or two, while the start of visible scooping motion is not.

Rounding: seconds values are the exact frame/fps quotient rounded to 3 decimals, EXCEPT the cycle, whose exact value is 25.1885 s. It is reported as 25.188 (not 25.189) so that the four rounded phase durations sum exactly to the rounded cycle duration.
known_caveats: ASYMMETRIC ONSET OFFSET. The digging onset at f125 uses +9 frames after first touch (~f116), but the cycle-closing onset at f880 uses a larger offset of ~+22 frames after its own first touch at ~f858. The two ends of the cycle therefore do not use the same convention. The ~13-frame difference (~0.43 s at 29.974 fps) is added to the labelled 'swinging' duration and to the labelled cycle duration, relative to what a symmetric convention would give. Both of those labels are therefore ~0.43 s long; 'digging', 'hauling' and 'dumping' are unaffected, because a shift applied to both ends of a phase cancels. With a +/-0.6 s tolerance this consumes most of the budget on two of the five fields, so a pipeline that is 'wrong' by ~0.4 s on swinging may in fact be using a more consistent convention than these labels do.
SINGLE CYCLE, SINGLE VIDEO. cycle_count is 1, so every 'average' here is an average over one sample. These labels say nothing about the pipeline's behaviour on multi-cycle or hidden videos.
The labels are one careful human's reading of ambiguous footage. Treat a sub-0.5 s disagreement as within labelling noise, not as a pipeline defect.
